title: Slow heat-driven flow in a gas of hard disks
authors: Amit Kumar, Abhishek Dhar, Baruch Meerson
abstract: We study a slow heat-driven flow in a gas of elastically colliding hard disks confined to a long channel. The initial state consists of two regions with large temperature and density contrasts but nearly equal pressures, leading to a low-Mach-number, nearly isobaric evolution. In the dilute limit, the corresponding isobaric hydrodynamic theory reduces to a previously known ideal-gas description. We extend this theory to finite densities by incorporating a non-ideal equation of state of a hard-disk fluid, and solve the resulting one-dimensional equations numerically. Finite-density effects produce appreciable deviations from the ideal-gas prediction. We then test the theory directly against event-driven molecular dynamics simulations of hard disks and find very good agreement in both the dilute and finite-density regimes. The results provide, to our knowledge, the first particle-level test of isobaric gas dynamics of a strongly inhomogeneous cooling flow.
summary: This work analyzes slow heat conduction in hard disk gases by coupling hydrodynamic theory with molecular dynamics simulations. The authors successfully extend the theoretical framework beyond the ideal gas limit to account for finite density effects using an appropriate equation of state. The strong agreement between theory and simulation validates the use of isobaric hydrodynamics for strongly inhomogeneous, low-Mach number cooling flows.
main_problem: The study investigates slow, heat-driven non-equilibrium flow in a gas of hard disks confined to a channel under nearly isobaric conditions.
main_result: The hydrodynamic theory, extended to finite densities using a hard-disk equation of state, shows excellent agreement with event-driven molecular dynamics simulations across both dilute and dense regimes.
method: The authors solve coupled one-dimensional partial differential equations derived from the low-Mach number isobaric heat-conduction formalism and compare these solutions against particle-level Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a gas of elastically colliding hard disks confined to a long channel, modeled using hydrodynamic equations that incorporate non-ideal equation of state corrections for finite densities.
key_observables: Temperature T(x, t), Density $\rho(x, t)$, Velocity $v(x, t)$, and Pressure $p(x, t)$.
important_parameters: Low Mach number regime; initial conditions featuring large temperature/density contrasts but nearly equal pressures ($p \approx 	ext{const}$).
main_assumptions: The flow is assumed to be low-Mach number (neglecting acoustic dynamics), and the theory extends from an ideal gas limit to finite densities using a specific equation of state.
figures_summary: Figures show self-similar scaling collapse of density, velocity, and temperature profiles when comparing MD data to hydrodynamic solutions; pressure plots confirm the system remains nearly isobaric over time.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the ideal gas limit theory, then extends it by incorporating a non-ideal equation of state for finite densities. The resulting 1D equations are solved numerically and validated against event-driven molecular dynamics simulations.
why_interesting: Although focused on classical fluid dynamics, the rigorous comparison between continuum hydrodynamics (derived from statistical principles) and microscopic particle simulations provides a powerful benchmark for developing non-equilibrium transport theories applicable to quantum systems.
